scenes.text: Did you know there is a fifty-square-mile strip of land in Yellowstone National Park where, due to a bizarre constitutional loophole, you might legally get away with murder?

The US Constitution clearly states you have the right to a jury from the exact state and district where the crime happened, but this specific part of Yellowstone is physically in Idaho while the entire park is legally governed by Wyoming.
This means your jury must be selected entirely from the Idaho portion of Yellowstone, which currently has a population of exactly zero, meaning a constitutional trial physically cannot happen.

While no one has actually tested this loophole yet, legal experts remain absolutely terrified of it. Would you ever dare to spend a night alone in this lawless zone? Subscribe and comment your thoughts below!
